notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VII.3.4.3 SR1: "If the CODE-SET clause is specified for a file, all data in that file must be described as USAGE IS DISPLAY and any signed numeric data must be described with the SIGN IS SEPARATE clause." Implemented at 85 for a file with record description entries: BindCodeSetClause records on FileModel.CodeSetRecordClass that the FD carries the clause, and the pass CheckCodeSetRecordItemsPass.Run, placed after sign and usage inheritance and with no edition arm, walks every written record through CheckCodeSetRecordItem and refuses with COBOL1672 each elementary item that is not usage DISPLAY and each signed numeric item whose effective SIGN clause is not SEPARATE. Probed at --std 85 beyond the witness (PIC S9(4) with no SIGN clause): SIGN LEADING and SIGN TRAILING without SEPARATE, a signed 01 elementary record, COMP, BINARY, PACKED-DECIMAL, a group USAGE COMPUTATIONAL, USAGE INDEX (elementary, level 01 and from a group), a second record, a REDEFINES item, an item under OCCURS and unnamed FILLER items are refused under STANDARD-1, STANDARD-2 and NATIVE alphabets; SIGN SEPARATE written on the item or on a containing group, unsigned numeric, alphabetic and edited items are accepted. Not implemented: a report file. Run walks FileModel.WrittenRecords only, and a report file has none (§1985:XIII.3.2.3 SR4), so the Report Section entries that describe the file's data are never screened; the pass follows the 2023 wording, which limits the rule to record description entries, where the 1985 rule covers all data in the file (the change record says so). The Report Writer file description entry prints the CODE-SET clause and takes its rules from this clause (§1985:XIII.3.2.4 GR3: "With the exception of the REPORT clause, all clauses within the file description entry for a report file shown on page XIII-7 are presented within the Sequential I-O module beginning on page VII-22."). So at --std 85 a report file with CODE-SET whose printable item is PIC S9(4) with no SIGN clause compiles, and the report line carries the over-punched sign character on a medium the clause says is converted.

next.reason: 1985: "If the CODE-SET clause is specified for a file, all data in that file must be described as USAGE IS DISPLAY"; 2023: "If there are record description entries associated with the file and no SELECT WHEN clauses are specified ... usage national". The 2023 display rule holds only when record entries exist and there is no SELECT WHEN; with alphabet-name-2 it requires usage national. 1985 required DISPLAY for all data, unconditionally.
